jobs.occupation: Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)
jobs.description:
Director Specialist – Key Account Management (Power & Controls)

Build strategic partnerships that power the future of renewable energy

At KK Group, we are on an ambitious journey to enable a future powered by renewable energy. We are looking for a commercially driven and relationship-oriented leader to take ownership of a key strategic account and help unlock its full potential.

In this role, you will work at the heart of our business—connecting customers, technology, and operations—to drive sustainable growth, strengthen long-term partnerships, and deliver real impact.

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark, Ikast

Responsibilities

Key Account Management:

• Obtain detailed knowledge of the account’s organization, their product portfolio, their on-going projects, and secure this is shared across commodities.

• Identify cooperation and sales opportunities

• Process customer RFQ’s and work cross-functionally with colleagues to generate the best technical and commercial offering

• Process ideas targeting increased business right from idea to implementation. Painstakingly drive the idea internally, build the business case and sell the new product or service

• Keep a strong and tight relationship with the Accounts’ technical and commercial organization and their internal stakeholders

• Contribute in development and adjustment of account strategy in order to support the overall business plan and targets for the account

• Support the customer on a day-to-day business

• Secure correct reporting, data and pipeline management in e.g. CRM

• Support all operational activities where sales need to be involved towards the customers to ensure highest level of performance.

• Drive customer negotiations to land new business and/or supporting the Key Account commodities across.

• Secure timely preparation, process and level of RFQ and negotiations across Key Account commodities and divisions.

Our requirements

We are looking for a commercially strong and collaborative professional who thrives in a global, customer-focused environment.

• 6-10 years of proven experience in Key Account Management within large OEM environments, with a proven ability to drive growth and create value for both the customer and the business

• A basic understanding of electromechanical components and industrial environments

• Strong commercial and financial acumen, with experience in budgeting, performance management, and delivering on business targets

• Excellent stakeholder management and negotiation skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and align expectations across internal and external partners

• Proven experience in leading cross-functional teams and managing complex projects in an industrial or technical environment

• A structured, analytical, and data-driven mindset, enabling you to translate insights into impactful decisions

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels in a global setting

• A collaborative and inclusive leadership style, with a commitment to safety, quality, and company values

• Cross-cultural awareness and the ability to operate effectively in an international matrix organisation

• Fluency in Danish and English (written and spoken); additional languages are considered a plus

Location

This role can be based in our offices in Ikast or Hammel, with flexibility for hybrid work.

Ready to make an impact?

If you are excited about shaping strategic partnerships and contributing to the renewable energy transition, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now & send us your resume in English.

Due to the summer vacation period in Denmark, all applications will be processed only in the beginning of August.

We offer

By joining KK Group, you will be part of a culture where diversity is embraced, every nationality is respected, and trust and collaboration across perspectives drives our success. Across our global organisation, we offer a wide range of job opportunities spanning office-based roles, production facilities, and onsite positions worldwide. Our roles cover multiple functions, locations, and disciplines, providing diverse career paths across the business. Whether you’re interested in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or support functions, you’ll find opportunities at KK Group to grow your skills, contribute to meaningful work, and make an impact.

Potential Benefits (Depending on Role)

Further information

If the above matches your field of interest and your qualifications, please send your application and resume as soon as possible. Interviews are held on an ongoing basis.

For further information, please contact:

Karen Lim  +45 4194 6883

About KK Group

KK Group is a global technology partner delivering power, controls, cooling, monitoring and service solutions for renewable energy and energy-intensive industries.

With more than 45 years of experience in the wind industry and technologies installed in over 120,000 turbines worldwide, KK Group provides critical electro-mechanical systems that enable electrification, improve energy efficiency, and optimise the lifetime performance of industrial assets.

The company’s capabilities span the full value chain - from development and manufacturing to service and digital solutions - supporting customers across the entire lifecycle of their platforms. Backed by its long-term owner, A.P. Moller Holding, KK Group is expanding beyond wind into selected energy-intensive industries including hydrogen, mining, rail and defence.

Today, KK Group employs more than 3,700 people across 10+ countries and is building a more diversified, resilient and global business - Powering Change towards a more sustainable tomorrow.

Visit www.kkgroup.com to learn more about our company and career opportunities.

jobs.occupation: System Manager, AC Skid – BESS (Medium Voltage Containerized Systems)
jobs.description:
System Manager, AC Skid – BESS (Medium Voltage Containerized Systems)

Shape the backbone of the energy transition

Are you passionate about building reliable, future-ready energy systems?

Do you enjoy working at the intersection of electrical engineering, system integration, and real-world impact?

Highlights of the offer

• Job offer expiration: 30/11/2026

• Type of work: Hybrid

• Role: Individual Contributor / Specialist

• Location: Europe, Denmark

Responsibilities

Serve as the overall system‑responsible owner for the AC Skid, covering electrical/functional architecture, safety, quality, and lifecycle performance.

Lead supplier selection, qualification, and governance for the mechanical Skid design, ensuring alignment with system requirements, standards, and cost targets.

Own the technical selection and specification of:

• MV transformer

• RMU

• PCS (in house designed converter integration and interfaces

Ensure correct electrical and functional integration of all subsystems:

• MV transformer – RMU – PCS

• Grounding/earthing

• Cooling and auxiliary power

• Cabling, interlocks, protections, and monitoring

Review and validate supplier designs for the mechanical skid

Ensure compliance with relevant standards:

• MV equipment (IEC/ANSI)

• Transformer and switchgear safety

• Environmental, mechanical, and fire safety

Review supplier documentation, test results, FAT reports, and qualification data.

Drive quality and cost optimization, ensuring a price‑competitive and high‑quality AC Skid product for the BESS platform.

Support customer clarification and quotation phases, ensuring:

• Technical feasibility

• Clear interpretation of customer requirements

• Alignment between project needs and AC Skid capabilities

Collaborate cross‑functionally with electrical, mechanical, controls, product, procurement, and quality teams to ensure seamless AC Skid integration.

Our requirements

Must‑haves:

Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Energy Engineering, or similar.

Strong understanding of:

• MV transformers, RMUs, switchgear, and MV safety

• Grid‑connected PCS/power converters

• MV protection, grounding/earthing, and interlocking

• Cooling and auxiliary systems

Experience working with suppliers on:

• Detailed mechanical design reviews

• Documentation review and compliance checks

• Quality and cost evaluations

Ability to support technical clarifications during pre‑sales and quotation phases.

Nice‑to‑haves:

Experience with AC Skids, E‑houses, containerized MV designs, or BESS systems.

Knowledge of grid code requirements for MV‑connected BESS or hybrid power plants.

Familiarity with DFMEA, FAT processes, and utility compliance documentation.

Background in system engineering or product ownership roles.

Location

Own the system. Shape the solution. Enable the energy transition.

• PCS (Power Conversion System)

• Understanding customer technical and functional requirements

• Clarifying integration, performance, and compliance aspects

Ensure the BESS platform meets all relevant standards and certifiable requirements for the targeted European and global markets.

Drive product-level requirement definition, functional specifications, technical governance, and change management.

Contribute to product roadmap development, ensuring alignment with market trends, grid requirements, and future hybrid power plant needs.

Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Energy Systems, Controls Engineering, or a related field.

Strong understanding of grid‑scale BESS architecture and system integration.

Understanding of grid interconnection requirements, certifiable standards, and BESS compliance guidelines.

Experience with customer technical discussions, system sizing, and solution definition.

Experience in hybrid power plant solutions (BESS + PV + WTG).

jobs.occupation: Warehouse employee (Full-time)
jobs.description:
Can you perform in a busy environment, do you have experience from packing or from a warehouse and do you have a good physique?

About the job

As a warehouse employee you are an important part of the business. You will pack products for our customers from refrigerated, dry, green and frost areas. We use pick-by-voice, and you will be walking around the warehouse, picking and packing orders throughout your entire shift. This requires that you have a good physique.

The packing department consists of more than 40 different nationalities and since it is a multicultural area it requires that you speak and understand English.

Work hours

Nemlig operates 365 days a year and you should be able to work in rotation, also during the afternoon, evenings and weekends. It is important that you are able to work in our different timeslot rotations, which depends on seasons and order flows. Please feel free to specify in your application which exact times that would work best for you.

Please note: As part of the recruitment process, selected candidates will be invited to an interview  at 10 am on a weekday (Tuesday or Wednesday) followed by additional onboarding sessions at 11 am on a weekday (Thursday or Friday), too. Therefore it is important you are available om weekdays in the daytime for interview and onboarding.

Availability to attend the interview and all scheduled onboarding sessions is a requirement for the position.

Our expectations

We hire responsible employees who thrive in a performance environment and who are willing to go the extra mile.

Furthermore, we expect that you:

• Have a good physique

• Keep calm - even in stressful situations

• Speak and understand English

• Can present a criminal record

Experience with single items picking, working in a warehouse environment and using pick-by voice systems is a plus, but not a requirement.

What do we offer

Our employees are the most important resource in the company why we are able to offer you the following:

• Collective agreement wage

• Pension scheme

• Health insurance

• Employee store with consumer goods and nice discounts

• Free delivery and 10% off on orders from nemlig.com

• Free gym open 24/7

Do you want to be our new colleague?

It is a requirement for you to be located in Denmark and to hold a Danish CPR-number, for us to be able to invite you for a possible interview.  If you have any questions, you are more than welcome to contact the Recruitment office at rekrutteringdrift@nemlig.com.

Apply for the job by pressing the link “søg stillingen”/ “apply” and answer the questionnaire. Please upload a picture of your EU passport or work permit (both sides) if you are not a danish citizen, if you have upploaded this we cannot process your application.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Vi har  åbent 365 dage om året, og kan med flere end 9.000 forskellige  varer opfylde alle indkøbsbehov. jobs.occupation: Mechanical Design Consultant - Robust Design
jobs.description:
Pls note that we do not support relocation or visa sponsorship for this position

Do you enjoy working through complex mechanical problems, questioning assumptions, and understanding why a design behaves the way it does?

At RD8, you will work hands-on with mechanical product development, using analysis and practical design work to solve challenging client problems. You will join an international team of mechanical engineers in a dedicated technical environment where specialist expertise is central to the work as part of a dynamic start-up

This role is for engineers who want to stay close to the engineering work and don’t shy away from the hard and interesting challenges where you have to use all of your toolbox

About RD8

We help companies that cannot afford to get it wrong make better engineering design decisions. Through consulting, software and ventures, we strengthen how mechanical R&D teams think, design and deliver.

Our aim is to make Robust Design an everyday engineering practice.

Our engineering ecosystem brings together specialist knowledge, training, documentation and software.

We work with R&D, operations and manufacturing organizations across industries, including major international companies, to make mechanical products less sensitive to variation.

What you will do

As a Robust Design Consultant, you will work directly on clients’ mechanical design challenges. You will investigate how parts interact, how tolerances affect function, and how designs can be improved.

The role combines engineering work with client dialogue and technical responsibility for project delivery.

• Work with small teams to design, analyse, and improve mechanical products. We work either inside our client’s teams or as more independent teams.

• Develop solutions for new products across several industries.

• Analyse and improve existing products in a range of industries.

• Create data-driven transparency in your solutions to improve decision-making.

• Explain findings and design recommendations to clients, help deliver projects, and coordinate technical work within the team.

You will be working on these tasks with frontrunners within the area of Robust Design - experts on a global level, in a start-up with global ambitions.

We are continuously developing our framework and adopting or creating solutions for our engineering ecosystem.

There’s a short way from decision to action and a high degree of freedom to shape the company and solutions. Great opportunities to take responsibility and for shaping business areas going forward

Your background

We welcome engineers with two or more years of relevant professional experience, ideally in mechanical product development, as well as senior specialists who want to deepen their expertise and remain hands-on.

• A master’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related field.

• Strong analytical skills across mechanical function, tolerance variation, and solid mechanics.

• Knowledge of Robust Design principles.

• Knowledge of production technologies and Design for Manufacturing (DFM).

• Fluent English.

Additional experience we value

• Working knowledge of statistical methods and finite element simulation methods.

• Experience with prototyping tools and methods.

• Strong communication and presentation skills.

• Danish or German language skills.

• Advanced simulation expertise.

Location and travel

This is a hybrid role based at our headquarters at Strandboulevarden 122, 3rd floor, 2100 Copenhagen, Denmark.

Expect 0–20 travel days per year.

Why join RD8

• Work alongside Robust Design specialists on mechanical challenges across products and industries.

• Have a high degree of freedom in how you approach your work and contribute to the methods and tools we develop.

• Flexibility to work from home when project and client commitments allow, with support for a home office setup

• Optional monthly social events, a subsidized lunch scheme and coffee, tea and snacks at the office.

• Take on responsibility and help shape our services and business areas as the company develops.

Apply

If you're a problem-solver who is excited about working on cutting-edge technology to create world-class solutions, then apply now with your CV

For further information about the position, contact Casper Høgh at csh@ing.dk

Please mention in your application that you saw the job on TechJob.

jobs.occupation: Student Worker in Controlling
jobs.description:
Student Worker in Controlling

Introduction

Are you data-curious, do you have a sharp eye for detail and do you want to kickstart your career in an international retail group with direct exposure to global controlling? Then you might be our new Working Student in Controlling!

We are seeking a structured and dependable Working Student (Junior Reporting Operations) to take full ownership of our daily management reporting routines and maintain high data quality across enterprise systems.

Your impact

In this role, you will play a crucial part in our day-to-day operations. You will manage regular reporting workflows, ensure data consistency, and transform BI insights into clear presentations for internal management. Additionally, you will serve as the operational bridge between our local business unit and international headquarters regarding governance and user access administration.

Meet your #teamlidl

You will join a vibrant, international team with direct exposure to global retail controlling practices. We prioritize community, professional growth, and maintaining a fun yet efficient working environment. Our communication culture is informal, and innovative ideas are always welcome—especially when it comes to automating and streamlining workflows.

About the job

Your workday will follow structured morning routines and a predictable rhythm, facilitating easy planning. jobs.occupation: Specialist, CMC Analytical Execution & Technology
jobs.description:
CMC Specialist for Analytical Execution & Technology

Job description

Location

Måløv, Denmark

Job category

Global Manufacturing & Supply

Your impact begins here

As CMC Specialist for Analytical Execution & Technology, you will strengthen the analytical methods that underpin the quality and performance of Novo Nordisk's drug products. Working within CMC Analysis & Characterization, you will lead scientific problem-solving, advance chromatographic and dissolution methods, and drive improvements in method robustness and data quality. Your expertise will shape how analytical challenges are resolved across the portfolio — creating tangible progress for people who depend on our medicines.

What you'll bring

• A PhD or master's degree in pharmaceutical sciences, engineering or another relevant natural science discipline.

• At least six years of experience in analytical development or a quality control environment.

• In-depth expertise in chromatographic methods, including UPLC and HPLC.

• An innovative and proactive mindset with the confidence to challenge established practices and advance method- and quality-related investigations.

• The ability to work both independently and collaboratively with a broad range of stakeholders, including Analytical Development, project offices and Quality Assurance/Regulatory Affairs.

• Strong communication skills — you can convey complex scientific insights clearly to diverse audiences and influence decisions through evidence-based reasoning.

• Fluency in written and spoken English.

On a personal level, you thrive in a collaborative scientific environment while confidently taking ownership of your area of expertise. You step forward when leadership is needed, adapt quickly to evolving priorities and data, and inspire others to engage with and act on your ideas.

What you'll do

You will deliver high-quality analytical outcomes and strengthen the methods that support Novo Nordisk's product portfolio. Your work will include:

• Providing subject-matter expertise in chromatographic methods, including UPLC and HPLC, as well as dissolution testing.

• Leading scientific troubleshooting and root-cause investigations to deliver timely, reliable analytical results.

• Challenging established approaches and driving improvements that strengthen method robustness, efficiency and data quality.

• Developing and updating analytical method strategies, including study plans, acceptance criteria and approaches to data interpretation that support differentiated quality.

• Mentoring and guiding colleagues and laboratory staff on experimental approaches, data interpretation and problem-solving.

• Collaborating across the value chain with experts in Analytical Development, Quality Assurance, Drug Development, CMC Pilots and quality control laboratories to translate analytical requirements into validated, high-quality methods.

Who you'll work with

You will join CMC Analytical Execution & Technology, a department within the CMC Analysis & Characterization (AnaC) area, located in Måløv. The department is approximately 130 colleagues organised in seven teams, all working within Good Scientific Practice (GSP) and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP). The culture is open-minded, collaborative and focused on delivering high-quality work and customer satisfaction.

As part of the CMC Development organisation within Product & Portfolio Strategy, your closest partners will include colleagues in Analytical Development, Quality Assurance, Drug Development, CMC Pilots and quality control laboratories. You will work across the Novo Nordisk value chain, combining perspectives and expertise to move analytical methods from development through validation to reliable results.

For more information about the role, please contact Tanni Leth Lundsager, Director, at tlc@novonordisk.com.

What you can expect here

You will join a dynamic scientific environment where your expertise shapes tangible outcomes — including methods that support the quality and performance of future drug products. The role offers clear development opportunities toward senior scientific leadership, technical authority responsibilities or project leadership within QC Analysis.

You will be supported through hands-on experience, cross-functional collaboration and opportunities to build new capabilities across the value chain. Your perspective matters: you will be trusted to take ownership, challenge the status quo and contribute to progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What we offer

At Novo Nordisk, you will join a global healthcare company with a distinctive culture and a strong track record. We offer continuous learning, career development and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary: The annual base salary for this role ranges from DKK 742,600 to DKK 1,091,600, depending on the level of the position. Placement within the range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and benefits: The compensation package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives, together with other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy: https://www.novonordisk.com/careers/working-at-novo-nordisk/total-rewards-benefits.html

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to bring your analytical expertise to a role where scientific quality drives real progress, apply for the CMC Specialist for Analytical Execution & Technology role by 27 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Site Manager – new biogas plants in Denmark and abroad
jobs.description:
Site Manager – new biogas plants in Denmark and abroad

Bigadan is built by people with deep professional expertise and a shared ambition: to create the circular energy solutions of the future. We have been building biogas plants for more than 40 years, in Denmark and abroad, and the coming years are busy. We have expansion and greenfield projects lined up in Denmark and Scandinavia, plus support projects for our clients in Germany and the UK. That is why we are looking for an experienced Site Manager for our Projects team.

Anywhere from 10 to 50+ people from different contractors on site, all needing to deliver at the same time. You are the one holding it all together. And when you hand over, you leave behind a plant that produces biogas for decades.

The role

You lead the site day to day from ground-breaking through commissioning and handover to operations. The people on site are mainly contractors in civil, mechanical, electrical, piping and process works. You report formally to Head of Projects Luke Morris, while Head of Site Managers Stefan Wussow is your manager in day-to-day operations. You work closely with the individual Project Managers and the Site team.

You spend around 80% of your time on site and 20% in the office. Our construction site office and workshop are based in Husum, Germany. Ideally, we would like you to be based in southern Denmark near Kliplev or Husum, but as the role involves a lot of travel, we are recruiting across Denmark and northern Germany. Our projects are spread across Denmark and abroad, including Sweden, Germany, Finland and the UK.

We expect you to be ready for periods of 3–4 weeks living near the site. Employment can be in Denmark or in Germany.

What you do

Site leadership. You coordinate daily activities and contractor progress, plan access, deliveries and lifting operations, and solve problems before they become delays.

Safety. You lead site inspections and toolbox talks and approve risk assessments and method statements. You set the standard on site.

Quality and documentation. You make sure the work follows drawings and specifications, including welding, and keep track of inspections and documentation.

Handover. You manage punch lists and close-out, so we hand over a plant that works from day one.

What makes this role specific

With us, you are not building for a client you will never see again. We operate the plants ourselves afterwards, and our own colleagues will live with what you build for many years. You succeed in this role when you have led the next builds safely to completion, made the right decisions along the way, kept the budget on track, and made both the collaboration and the construction succeed.

We imagine that you:

• have a technical education, e.g. as a mechanical engineer, or a trade background (civil, mechanical or electrical) with hands-on experience

• have at least 5 years' experience as a site manager on industrial, energy, utility or process projects

• know civil, mechanical and electrical works and the health and safety rules on a construction site

• speak and write English and either Danish or German

Experience in biogas or anaerobic digestion is an advantage, but not a requirement. It is also an advantage if you hold a Danish construction safety coordinator certificate (AMK-B), first aid, knowledge of ATEX zones, or experience with welding coordination.

As a person, you are visible on site and make decisions when they need to be made. You can push back on a contractor and still have a good working relationship the next day.

We offer

A central role in a growing company, where you are involved from ground-breaking until the plant is running. You get a competitive salary, either mileage at the official Danish rates or a company van, accommodation and per diem on projects, pension and health insurance, ongoing training and support for relevant certifications. The position is full-time, starting 1 February or 1 March 2027.

About Bigadan

We develop, build, operate and own biogas plants and work across the entire value chain, from sourcing organic residues to producing energy, biogenic CO₂ and biofertiliser. We are around 200 colleagues and have built more than 40 biogas plants in Denmark and abroad.

Every day, we turn manure, food waste and other organic residues into products of value for the energy, agriculture and industrial sectors. This supports security of supply, makes better use of resources and returns nutrients to the soil.

Interested?

The application deadline is Wednesday 30 December 2026. We hold interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your application and CV as soon as possible. If you have questions, please contact Head of Projects Luke Morris on +45 3073 6851 or lm@bigadan.dk.
